pipelines.name: The review loop
steps: a reviewer marks, comments and decides in the player, then presses Finish: approve, or request changes
the review server keeps the review in the inbox and hands it to a waiting session, or starts the headless run
reel record adds the answers to the decision log and files the review, with what to act on
the revise step folds the comments into the plan, or rewrites only the steps they touched
narrate voices only the changed lines, finish-project reassembles the video, and plan-diff flags what changed
a notification says the video is ready, and the player plays just the changes

pipelines.name: The build loop
steps: the implement step builds from the approved plan and logs every call the plan did not cover, tagging the ones a reviewer might overturn
a second agent checks the diff against the plan and the ledger
the walkthrough video shows each change running and pauses at the calls reel stops names; the others are one list at the end
the reviewer accepts or requests changes, and the review reaches the agent as in the review loop
the walkthrough fix step changes what was flagged and, when changes were requested, rebuilds only those beats
spec.md is updated and the system video rebuilds only the frames it affects

stage.why: reelplanning is two loops over the same parts, and only a graph with return edges can show a loop. The edges are real hand-offs, each carrying something to the next part (the review, the inbox row, reviews/<kind>-<time>.md, the script, the video). The review loop runs round the outside: along the top from the review server to the revise step, down the right to finish-project, back along the bottom to plan-diff and up to the review player. The build loop starts inside, at the implement step, and takes the same path, with the walkthrough fix step in place of the revise step. The headless run sits on the review's path because a review nobody is waiting for goes through it; a session that is waiting takes it instead. The system video hangs off the reel CLI above the top row, and the plan-to-video skill, which makes every video but hands no file along an edge, stands apart beside it.
